To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the AlGaN/GaN EGFETs are suitable for the analysis of ion channel activity of living cells.

the EGFETs can be successfully used to study the response of the NG108- 15 cells to DFP, and that the EGFETS have the potential for use as a tool to monitor the response of nerve cells to chemical stimuli.
the AlGaN/GaN EGFET is suitable for real-time detection of nerve cells response to serine hydolase inhibitors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an EGFET sensor for the analysis of the activity of nerve cells.
the development of a novel biosensor based on an AlGaN/GaN EGFET for the detection and quantification of nerve cell activity.
the development of a novel type of biocompatible, optically transparent and biologically functionalized sensor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AlGaN/GaN based electrolyte gated field effect transistor (AlGaN/ GaN based EGFET) has been successfully developed for monitoring the nerve cell activity.
the AlGaN/GaN sensor material is biocompatible and can be used in cell-based biosensors.
the sensor can be used to monitor the response of the nerve cells to the inhibitor and the inhibitor can be detected in a very short time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we could demonstrate the biocompatibility and the functionality of the sensor material and we have shown that the inhibitor can be monitored with the sensor.
we have demonstrated a novel approach for the detection of inhibitors by using a neuron transistor coupling.
the EGFET is a suitable tool to study the response of nerve cells to inhibitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to monitor nerve cell responses with the AlGaN/GaN EGFET sensor.
the sensor material is biocompatible with nerve cells and the EGFET is a suitable tool for monitoring the response of the cells to inhibitors.
the sensor can be used to monitor the activity of ion channels in the membrane of nerve cells.
